study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Oliveira-Saraiva and Ferreira, Frontiers in Psychiatry, 2023
study_identification_part.si4_title: Normative model detects abnormal functional connectivity in psychiatric disorders

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The paper states clear objectives and the purpose of applying normative modeling. They aim to investigate whether a normative model based on functional connectivity can discriminate psychiatric disorders and address heterogeneity. The abstract and introduction explicitly describe proposing a normative model using autoencoders and its intended diagnostic relevance.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "We trained our autoencoder on resting-state fMRI... The model was then tested on schizophrenia (SCZ), bipolar disorder (BD), and attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) patients to estimate how each patient deviated from the norm..."; "In this study, we aim to investigate if normative models based on functional connectivity are able to discriminate against different psychiatric disorders... Therefore, we propose a normative model based on autoencoders..."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: This study builds a new normative model on healthy individuals. Eligibility and data quality criteria are described: they restricted inclusion to age 18–50, TR=2s, eyes open; applied motion/exclusion thresholds (framewise displacement >3 mm, translation >3 mm, angular deviation >3°) and removed subjects accordingly; final healthy sample counts per set are reported (H-Train n=366, H-Test-U n=39, H-Test-C n=70), and reasons for exclusion include motion and missing images.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "We established an age range between 18 and 50 years old, a repetition time (TR) of 2 s, and we only included subjects who underwent the MRI scanner with their eyes open."; "data in which the maximum framewise displacement exceeded 3 mm, motion in translation exceeded 3 mm, or angular deviation exceeded 3° were excluded... Following these criteria, 32 subjects were removed... it was not possible to finish data preprocessing for several subjects due to the lack of a rs-fMRI image or T1-weighted image."; "H-Train represents the 366 healthy subjects... H-Test-U is the set of 39 healthy subjects... H-Test-C ... 70 healthy subjects..."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and sex were not modeled as covariates in the autoencoder (explicitly acknowledged). Some sources of variability were mitigated by selection constraints (age range, TR, eyes open) but no explicit covariate adjustment or site harmonization (e.g., ComBat, hierarchical modeling) is described.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "Fourthly, we started with a simple autoencoder that received no information about sex/age."; "We established an age range between 18 and 50 years old, a repetition time (TR) of 2 s, and we only included subjects who underwent the MRI scanner with their eyes open."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Secondary data from existing public datasets were used; per guide, acquisition protocol details are not required (answer NA for SECONDARY data).

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing is described with software and steps: ANTs brain extraction; FSL MELODIC for initial steps (discard first volumes, motion correction via MCFLIRT, smoothing, high-pass filtering, ICA); FIX for denoising; registration (BBR to T1, non-linear to MNI); dual regression using a 14-network template; QC thresholds are specified.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "brain extraction of the T1-weighted images ... using the Advanced Normalization Tools (ANTs)."; "pre-processing of rs-fMRI images was handled within the FMRIB Software Library (FSL)... discard the first four volumes... motion correction using the MCFLIRT tool... spatial smoothing... highpass filter... single-session spatial independent component analysis (ICA)..."; "FMRIB's ICA-based Xnoiseifier (FIX) was applied to automatically detect and remove non-brain signal components..."; "registration to the individual T1-weighted structural image through the boundary-based registration (BBR)... then to the MNI152 standard space..."; "dual regression was applied. We used the fourteen FBNs from Shirer et al. as a template..."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: They used ten-fold cross-validation on the training data to validate and optimize the model, ensuring evaluation on samples not used for fitting in each iteration.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "Ten fold cross-validation was applied to validate the optimized model while studying its generalization. The model was trained and tested ten times, using a different fold as the validation set in each time."

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: They applied the trained normative model to an independent external dataset (COBRE), including a healthy cohort (H-Test-C) not used for model development.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "In the end, the normative model was tested on an independent dataset, COBRE."; "H-Test-C and SCZ-Test-C are the independent test sets consisting of 70 healthy subjects, and 49 SCZ patients from the COBRE dataset, respectively."

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach is a deep autoencoder; they specify architecture (hidden layers 91-46-1346-91), activation (leaky ReLU), regularization (L2), dropout (0.5), loss (MSE), initialization (He), training epochs (1000), optimizer (Adam with parameters), and implementation software (Keras Python library).
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "Autoencoder was the selected architecture... implemented using the Keras Python library."; "The model that better balanced both normalized metrics was selected for training. It consisted of three hidden layers (91-46-1346-91)... L2 regularization... dropout 0.5... mean squared error ... He initialization... trained for 1,000 epochs, using Adam optimization (β1 = 0.9, β2 = 0.999, ε = 1e-7, learning rate 0.0005)."

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: They report quantitative performance metrics: subject-level reconstruction error (MSEs) distributions and statistical significance via Mann–Whitney tests showing healthy vs patient group differences; cross-validation metrics used for model selection are also described.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "The MSEs were calculated for each subject, and boxplots were generated..."; "Considering a p = 0.05, it is noticeable that the differences between the groups of patients and the healthy subjects are statistically significant."; "The mean of the median MSEs values of the training set for the 10 folds of cross-validation... were calculated for optimizing the model."

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: They define deviation scores as reconstruction error (MSEs) and absolute differences between reconstructed and input connectivity features. They specify a thresholding approach (top 20% of differences) to binarize abnormal connections for graph analysis. Clinical implications are discussed: disorder-specific abnormal connectivity patterns are identified; heterogeneity at the individual level suggests precision medicine utility.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: "The absolute difference between the output vector and the input vector was calculated... reshaped into a 14×14... and binarized using the threshold that is defined in the results section."; "For defining the threshold, we ... considered the 20% higher values of the merged vector... retained ... pairs of FBNs that were worse reconstructed... probably functionally abnormal."; "The results demonstrate that the proposed model could identify functional connectivity patterns that characterize different psychiatric disorders... However, the group-level differences did not withstand individual-level analysis... These findings suggest that a precision-based medical approach... may be more beneficial..."
